The current scenario is that a large part of the current species will disappear in the next 200 years.The current extinction rates are about 100 times higher than the background ones, and growing.

Note that the extinction rates are different in different species groups (as far as we know), the mammals and birds are the ones going away the fastest.

The evidence is incontrovertible that recent extinction rates are unprecedented in human history and highly unusual in Earth’s history. Our analysis emphasizes that our global society has started to destroy species of other organisms at an accelerating rate, initiating a mass extinction episode unparalleled for 65 million years. If the currently elevated extinction pace is allowed to continue, humans will soon (in as little as three human lifetimes) be deprived of many biodiversity benefits. On human time scales, this loss would be effectively permanent because in the aftermath of past mass extinctions, the living world took hundreds of thousands to millions of years to rediversify. Avoiding a true sixth mass extinction will require rapid, greatly intensified efforts to conserve already threatened species and to alleviate pressures on their populations—notably habitat loss, overexploitation for economic gain, and climate change (31–33). All of these are related to human population size and growth, which increases consumption (especially among the rich), and economic inequity (6). However, the window of opportunity is rapidly closing.

http://advances.sciencemag.org/content/1/5/e1400253.full

Personally I don't think there's much to do, one problem is that the population dynamic is slow; it has a lot of inertia, and each human requires a minimum surface of land to survive. Chaos or collapse will probably not help either.
I would say, that no matter what, probability is against us living on only one planet. One way or another our home will be destroyed.

I totally agree. On a long enough time line, Earth is inevitably going to be slapped by an "Extinction-Level Event" sized asteroid. I firmly believe that our future lies in colonized multiple planets, and maybe/hopefully large space stations, eventually.
Do you think we could be capable of sustainable living on those planets or would we just drain them of resources and move on?

Well, I guess it depends upon what we find on other planets. I would guess that each planet may come with its own unique set of resources. We may even discover a new resource that would be much more quickly renewable. Or, if a planet doesn't host any other life besides us, I guess there's no harm in depleting it of its resources?

Perhaps a more likely answer is that by the time we're out there colonizing and traveling between planets, we'll be a lot better at harnessing the power of the sun. I would definitely hope so, at least.
we need to plant minimum 2 trillion trees, preferably 5 trillion in the next 100 years to replace the ones we cut down. Indonesia, South America are most urgent.

Is there any evidence that what we're doing now would be enough or is it just mindless optimism?

We need to do something, while it certainly is not enough, it's better than nothing.

I feel like a lot of people need some sort of wake up call. Especially the ones behind powerful industries. They need to realize that the planet is worth more than money. The thing is, green technology is a good "half" solution. It's not something that will fix the problem, but more a necessity to fix it. The problem is that it requires an investment, it will perhaps be a big one, but certainly not an impossible one. I'm willing to bet that if the big nations collaborated, all the resources needed to power the world on green energy would be available.

Like I said, it's only half a solution, it won't solve the problem. The other part requires our way of life to change into a more ecological way, i.e. we need to tone down our consumption and waste. If not less waste, then even more and better recycling. I've seen projects like building city farms, vertical farms. These are all things that could help us.

Now (imo) the most important part. We as humans, need a big mentality change. I feel like our civilization is built on trial and error. E.g. earthquake takes down your house, you build a earthquake resistant house. You apply what works best. The thing is, we can't do that with the planet. There won't be a "Oh, we fucked up big time, well we'll do better next time". (Unless we find a earth like planet that could support life and we move there, but what are the odds). We don't need to change our way of life after we fuck up, but before. A few people living as ecological as possible is useless. They're doing a good thing, which I have enormous respect for, and it will make them feel better (I hope), but the impact is negligible. If we want to avoid extinction we'll need a majority of people changing their lives.

On to the big mentality change I mentioned. I haven't quite yet figured it out, but I have a feeling that we need to get rid of the "more is better" idea-thing. I feel like we have become addicted to money. But we can't really blame anyone, can we? It has become a necessity for survival. We created our capitalistic society, and now, we're its prey. I'm not saying that we should switch to communism (which imo is just disguised capitalism) or w/e, but I guess we should look for something new, and take the well-being of our planet into consideration this time.

tl;dr we need to change

Anyway those are my thoughts about it, for now.
